solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: (& 15ac.) Pubic hair in settee removed with lint (not A1) — cynical excuse for tabloid exposé?

indicators.note: read as re-moved, the letters are moved about into a fresh order
the bracketed 'not' tells the solver to leave out the following pair from the jumbled heap

parts.note: taken letter for letter as raw material
added to the pile as written
the letter A and the digit 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A lurid tale of pubic hair found in a sofa, with a dig at the excuses tabloids give for printing such stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: Take one A and one I out of the twenty-one letters of the first five words, then rearrange the nineteen left to get IN THE PUBLIC INTEREST.
explanation.definitionFit: Editors routinely claim a story serves society's right to know, a justification often seen as a cynical cover for prurient reporting.

clue.text: Curious git, splattered with urine on date

indicators.note: something splattered is spread about messily, so these letters get scattered into a new order

parts.note: the words git and urine supply the letters to be mixed
D is the standard abbreviation for date

explanation.surface: A crude image of an inquisitive idiot getting sprayed with urine on a night out.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone intrigued has had their interest aroused, which is the same state as being curious.

clue.text: Blair's left-wing members hit back — a real gem!

parts.note: Blair is Tony; the left-hand half of his first name supplies its two leftmost letters

indicators.note: hitting back here means the word for hit is read in the opposite direction, upward in this down light

parts.note: to zap is to hit or strike

explanation.surface: Old Labour stalwarts finally retaliate against Tony Blair, and the satirist cheers them as a real gem.
explanation.walkthrough: Blair's first name is Tony, and its 'left wing' is the left half of that name, not the party's socialists.
explanation.definitionFit: Topaz is a precious stone, so it is literally a genuine gem.

clue.text: Rep's buggered by sex's dynamic quality

indicators.note: something buggered is broken and messed up, so the letters come out in a wrecked order

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored
it is old slang for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: A salesman is ruined by a sex scandal, with the clue leering about his vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: IT for sex appeal is a crossword favourite, from the 1927 film 'It' starring Clara Bow.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit is lively spirit and wit, a borrowed French word for a vivacious, energetic character.

clue.text: Getting an erection? Revolting activity!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: rising up, read crudely
second meaning: a rebellion against authority

explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' looks like 'disgusting', which seems to follow from the first half, but it means rebelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Uprising means both the act of rising up and a popular revolt or insurrection.

clue.text: Food not touched, amphibian interrupts shaggers?

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: shagging is British slang for having sex, so shaggers are lovers
an eft is a newt, a small amphibian

explanation.surface: A couple's dinner goes uneaten because a newt crawls in on them mid-romp.
explanation.definitionFit: Leftovers are the remains of a meal that nobody ate, so they are food left untouched.

clue.text: Almost the last repository for our shit currency

definitions.text: Almost the last repository for our shit
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the large bowel, the stretch just before the rectum
second meaning: the monetary unit of Costa Rica (and formerly El Salvador)

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like a jibe that the nation's money is worthless; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The colon is the bowel section where waste is stored before the rectum, and the colón is also a Central American monetary unit.

clue.text: Snoop's organ has unnatural hair

parts.note: the ear is the organ of hearing
a wig is false hair

explanation.surface: Gossip about a nosy person whose body part sports some odd growth of hair.
explanation.walkthrough: Snoop is a verb here, not a nosy person, and 's stands for 'is'. EAR followed by WIG gives EARWIG.
explanation.definitionFit: To earwig is British slang for eavesdropping on a conversation, which is a form of prying.

clue.text: One who dictated "After head swing your chopper up"?

indicators.note: in a down light, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: the top is the head of something
to lop is to chop with a swing of an axe

explanation.surface: Gruesome dictated orders: once the head is off, raise your axe, with a smutty hint in 'chopper'.
explanation.walkthrough: Pol Pot led the Khmer Rouge regime that slaughtered huge numbers of Cambodians, fitting the beheading surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Pol Pot was the Cambodian dictator, so he is literally someone who ruled by dictating.

clue.text: Bill wants lay to turn over and misbehave

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

indicators.note: turning something over flips it, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to lay something down is to put it

explanation.surface: Bill wants his partner to roll over in bed and get naughty.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like a man's name, but here it is an account.
explanation.definitionFit: To act up is an idiom for behaving badly, especially of children or machines playing up.

clue.text: Minister might not have this drink of oil, being pissed

parts.note: port is a fortified wine

indicators.note: pissed is British slang for drunk, and drunken letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A government minister gets drunk on something unspeakable, a drink of oil.
explanation.walkthrough: A minister without portfolio is a cabinet member with no department to run.
explanation.definitionFit: A portfolio is a minister's area of responsibility, and some cabinet posts carry none.

clue.text: Brattish high fliers wish to get screwed holding snoring Josh

indicators.note: holding means wrapping around something else, so other letters go inside
something screwed is twisted out of shape, so the word is jumbled

parts.note: these letters are rearranged
ZZ is the cartoon sign of someone snoring
to josh is to kid, to tease

explanation.surface: Spoilt young achievers wish to bed a dozing man called Josh.
explanation.walkthrough: Josh looks like a name, but it is the verb meaning tease.
explanation.definitionFit: Whizz kids are young people who achieve great success quickly, often with a cocky manner.

clue.text: Acknowledge Gordon, without Blair, extremely happy!

indicators.note: without means lacking, so some letters are taken away from the surname

parts.note: Gordon Brown, Blair's successor as Labour prime minister

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the name
up means cheerful, in high spirits

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown has to admit he is delighted to be rid of Tony Blair.
explanation.walkthrough: BROWN minus B and R, the outer letters of Blair, leaves OWN; add UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up is to confess or admit something, which is to acknowledge it.

clue.text: Dwarf bloke with middle dropped over arse

indicators.note: lying over something covers it on both sides, so one part goes round the other
dropping the middle keeps only the two ends of the word

parts.note: a bloke is a guy; only its outer letters stay
the rump is the backside

explanation.surface: A short man, his trousers dropped, bending over his backside.
explanation.walkthrough: Grumpy is one of the seven dwarfs in Disney's Snow White.
explanation.definitionFit: Grumpy is a named character among Snow White's seven dwarfs, so he is an example of a dwarf.

clue.text: Do row, as cowed MPs stand by

definitions.note: a description: the thing that cowed MPs stand by

parts.note: a do is a party
a row is a line

explanation.surface: A party argument while timid MPs merely look on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel and 'stand by' suggests looking on, but row is a line and stand by means remain loyal to.
explanation.definitionFit: The party line is the official policy that obedient, whipped members are expected to support.

clue.text: see 1ac.
A donor's thing: a large penis?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a gift of money given to fund an institution
second meaning: what a well-endowed man has

explanation.walkthrough: 'Donor' suggests a sperm donor, steering both halves toward anatomy; the first is in fact a charitable gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefactor's lasting gift is an endowment, and 'well endowed' is a jokey phrase for a man with a large member.

clue.text: Inject energy into grossly fat UK or lose it

indicators.note: injecting puts something inside, so one letter goes into the following words
grossly means crudely and badly, so the letters are mangled into a new order

parts.note: these letters are jumbled
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A choice for an obese Britain: get some vigour into yourself or go to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'or' looks like the link word between the two halves, but its letters belong to the fodder too: E goes into FAT UK OR and the lot is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To freak out is an informal idiom for losing self-control in panic or anger, which is what losing it means.

clue.text: Sort of stroke beneath member

parts.note: beneath means under
an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A suggestive hint at a stroke below a man's member.
explanation.walkthrough: In this magazine, 'member' and 'stroke' are steered toward smut, but member means limb and stroke is a sporting shot.
explanation.definitionFit: An underarm shot is played with the hand below the shoulder, as in bowling or serving in cricket and tennis.

clue.text: Pretentious United player initially knocked back drink hard

parts.note: U is the usual abbreviation for United in team names

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the first letter of the word

indicators.note: knocked back here means turned backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to sip is to drink a little
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A Manchester United footballer downs a stiff drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back drink' reads as gulping alcohol, but it reverses SIP to PIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppish is a British informal word for arrogant or snobbish, which overlaps with pretentious.

clue.text: President's assistants suppressing small luvvy's whispers?

indicators.note: suppressing means holding something down inside, so one part is enclosed

parts.note: a president's helpers are his aides
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: White House staff hush up a theatrical type.
explanation.walkthrough: A luvvy is British slang for a gushing actor; the question mark flags that stage asides are not really whispered.
explanation.definitionFit: An aside is a remark an actor speaks to the audience as though unheard by other characters, like a stage whisper.

clue.text: Doing a peeping Tom in grass round outskirts of Putney

indicators.note: going round something encircles it, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: to grass and to sing both mean to inform on someone to the police

indicators.note: outskirts are the edges, so only the outer letters of the place name are kept

parts.note: Putney is a district of south-west London

explanation.surface: A voyeur lurks in the grass on the edge of Putney, a district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Grass looks like the lawn where the voyeur hides, but it is slang for informing, as is sing.
explanation.definitionFit: A peeping Tom watches people secretly, so behaving like one is spying.

clue.text: Slut rubbished Brenda's provincial place

indicators.note: rubbished means trashed and wrecked, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: these letters are jumbled
Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, whose royal cipher is ER

explanation.surface: Someone trashes the Queen's out-of-the-way home in rude terms.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye calls the late Queen Elizabeth 'Brenda'; ER is her Elizabeth Regina cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulster is one of the four historic provinces of Ireland, and the usual name for Northern Ireland, a part of the Queen's realm.

clue.text: see 27ac.
Arse cracks split by one cause an erection

indicators.note: being split by something means it is wedged in the middle
something that cracks breaks apart, so its letters fall into a new order

parts.note: these letters are rearranged
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A crude picture of someone's buttocks being enough to arouse.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something is to make it stand up, so in this smutty sense it means causing an erection.

clue.text: One Labour leader getting disgustingly wealthy as far as is possible

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: disgustingly suggests something made foul and messy, so these letters are scrambled
the leader of a word is the letter at its head

parts.note: the first letter of the party name
these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dig at a Labour leader who made a great fortune, taken to its limit.
explanation.definitionFit: All the way is an idiom for completely, to the furthest extent, so as far as one can go.

clue.text: Hot, unfocussed, very lacking cabinet member

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: lacking means without, so a letter is removed from the preceding word

parts.note: unfocused means vague, blurred
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A flustered, woolly-minded politician, very much lacking, is mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: William Hague was a Conservative party leader and later a cabinet minister.
explanation.definitionFit: William Hague served in the cabinet as Foreign Secretary, so he is an example of a cabinet member.

clue.text: Admit unhesitatingly it's how to show distaste after a blow job

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an urging to come out and say something

definitions.text: it's how to show distaste after a blow job
definitions.meaning: second meaning: literally ejecting something from the mouth

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is both an idiom urging someone to say what they mean and a literal description of getting rid of something from the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling someone to say something straight out is an idiom for confessing without hesitation; ejecting from the mouth signals dislike.

clue.text: (& 22ac.) It has one member at Westminster (resentful member, unknown)

definitions.text: It has one member at Westminster

parts.note: green with envy means resentful
a member is a part of a whole
Y is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: A dig at a lone MP sitting in Parliament, resentful and obscure.
explanation.walkthrough: When this ran, Caroline Lucas was the Green Party's only MP in the House of Commons at Westminster.
explanation.definitionFit: The Green Party held a single parliamentary seat, so it is the party described by one sitting MP.

clue.text: In the Common Market, Jack "not finished" Conservative arse's way of expelling high fliers

indicators.note: in places one item inside the letters of the next term

parts.note: the European Economic Community, the old name for the EU's forerunner
J is the abbreviation for jack in playing cards

indicators.note: something not finished lacks its end, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party
the seat is the backside

explanation.surface: A Eurosceptic jibe: a Tory MP's bottom gets him booted out of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not finished' sits in quotes after Jack as if it were his nickname, but it cuts the last letter from TORY.
explanation.definitionFit: An ejector seat fires a pilot out of a stricken aircraft, so it is a means of expelling airmen.
